examples.name: Kumamoto earthquake — Mayuyama (Japan)
examples.description: Mj7.1, 28 Jul 2026 — slope failure above Shimabara, seen 6 days later
examples._verified: 2026-08-04 live Earth Search: grid MGRS-52SFB (EPSG:32652); A=S2B_52SFB_20250729_0_L2A (cloud 1.5%), B=S2B_52SFB_20260803_0_L2A (cloud 15.9%); 2 usable A / 1 usable B scenes on the winning grid (A alternate S2C_52SFB_20250724_0_L2A). SCL clear-sky over this bbox: A 100.0%, B 100.0%, 100.0% jointly clear. Offline replay of the same pipeline at 10 m (threshold 0.15, min area 0.5 ha) yields 85 patches / 168.8 ha; largest 51.96 ha at 32.76516N 130.34420E = the new bare-ground scar on the south-east flank of Mt Mayuyama, continuous forest in A; second 34.96 ha at 32.75413N 130.33009E = the Mizunashi-gawa sabo works below Fugendake, where ongoing earthworks (not necessarily the earthquake) strip the recolonized 1991-95 pyroclastic deposit. Dating: the Mayuyama scar is already present on 2026-07-29, the first Sentinel-2 pass after the event (~19 h later, seen through thin cloud), but the site was overcast on every 2026 pre-event pass — clear fraction over the 1.1x1.1 km scar footprint was 2.5% on 07-14, 12.1% on 07-21 and 0.0% on 07-24 — so the last clean pre-event view is 2025-07-29 and the imagery alone brackets the failure to that 12-month interval.
examples._notes: Dates are deliberate. (a) The +-5-day B window spans 2026-07-29..08-08, so it cannot reach back past the 2026-07-28 16:27 JST event; the pairer picks the *clearest* scene in the window, not the nearest, so a wider window risks silently selecting a pre-event scene as B. (b) A is the same season one year earlier (both late July), so vegetation phenology largely cancels. The Kumamoto-side epicentral damage (buildings, bridges, liquefaction, fires) is not detectable by 10 m NDVI; an epicentral AOI [130.58,32.52,130.78,32.72] was tested (97.6% jointly clear, so it is a usable alternative if you want the epicentre itself) and its largest patches were golf-course turf that browned and a new construction site — neither attributable to the earthquake from imagery alone. Mt Mayuyama, which the reports name as a genuine slope collapse, is the one satellite-visible surface failure of this event. Caveat: the pipeline has no per-pixel cloud/shadow mask (SCL is not read), and a year of construction and forestry sits in the baseline alongside the earthquake.

examples.name: Rasuwa flood — Trishuli at Betrawati (Nepal)
examples.description: Ice-rock avalanche surge, 26 Aug 2026 — Trishuli channel scour, seen next day
examples._verified: 2026-08-31 live Earth Search: grid MGRS-45RUM (EPSG:32645); A=S2C_45RUM_20260812_0_L2A (cloud 18.7%), B=S2B_45RUM_20260827_0_L2A (cloud 78.5%); 1 usable A / 1 usable B scene on the winning grid, so both alternate dropdowns are empty. MGRS-45RUL is the only other grid this bbox returns and it would otherwise WIN the combined-cloud argmin (27.9+54.3=82.2 against RUM's 18.7+78.5=97.2), but it is dropped on both dates by the hard-coded 10% nodata gate (s2:nodata_pixel_percentage 31.4% on 08-12, 30.9% on 08-27), leaving RUM uncontested. SCL clear-sky over this bbox: A 99.9%, B 92.1%, 92.0% jointly clear (B also carries 3.2% cloud and 3.5% cloud shadow); the AOI is 100% valid data on both dates. Offline replay of the same pipeline at 10 m (level 0, 402x506 px window, threshold 0.15, min area 0.5 ha) yields 20 patches / 273.7 ha. Largest 87.07 ha at 27.95905N 85.17245E = a 5.1 km ribbon of scoured Trishuli valley floor (shape fill 0.04, i.e. a channel-following strip rather than a blob; SCL vegetation 76% / bare 21% on 08-12 becomes bare 78% / water 8% / dark 13% on 08-27; mean NDVI 0.63 -> -0.05). Second 48.95 ha at 27.93963N 85.15623E and third 42.88 ha at 27.96366N 85.17133E are the same scour swath downstream and upstream, 99-100% clear-sky and within 0.5 km of the channel; fifth 16.25 ha at 27.97311N 85.18199E lies directly on the river at Betrawati. The 20 patches partition exactly: 206.92 ha across 8 patches passes both tests used here (SCL-clear fraction >= 0.85 AND centroid within 800 m of the Trishuli channel) and is read as flood scour; 54.86 ha across 8 patches has an SCL-clear fraction below 0.5 and is cloud/shadow artifact, the four largest being #4 (27.50 ha), #6 (15.35 ha), #9 (4.18 ha) and #10 (2.44 ha) at 49.47 ha between them; the remaining 11.96 ha across 4 patches is clear-sky but off-channel or shallow-drop, dominated by #7 at 9.12 ha (27.96024N 85.18530E, SCL-clear 0.93, 0.88 km off-channel, NDVI drop only 0.38 and still 64% vegetation in B) which is most likely harvest or phenology, not flood. 206.92 + 54.86 + 11.96 = 273.74. The cloud/shadow share survives because the pipeline applies no per-pixel mask. Independent SCL cross-check, using no NDVI at all: unvegetated ground (SCL bare + water) over the whole 2034 ha bbox rises from 5.15% to 12.91% between 12 and 27 Aug, about 158 ha of newly stripped surface in fifteen days.
examples._notes: Dates are deliberate. (a) The +-2-day B window spans 2026-08-27..08-31, whose lower bound is exactly the first post-event pass, so it cannot reach back past the 2026-08-26 02:52 UTC collapse; the last pre-event acquisition over this tile was 08-24, one day outside. This matters because the pairer picks the *clearest* scene in the window, not the nearest, and the counterfactual was run live rather than assumed: a +-5-day window (08-24..09-03) returns S2A_45RUM_20260824_1_L2A at 50.97% cloud and 8.69% nodata, i.e. fully usable and much clearer than the 78.47% scene we want, so cloud-ascending order would have silently selected a PRE-event image as B and the preset would have reported almost nothing. windowDays 3 is the largest safe value here; 2 is used for margin. dateB is a search centre, not the scene date: the only post-event scene in the catalogue as of today is 08-27, and the 08-29 one (cloud 82.6%) is dropped by the nodata gate at 43.1%. (b) The +-2-day A window spans 08-10..08-14 and contains three other acquisitions (08-11, and two on 08-14), but all three are edge-of-swath and gated out at 43-69% nodata, so A resolves to 2026-08-12 on cloud (18.7%) and on nodata independently — the pair is doubly forced. (c) The baseline is the same-season scene fifteen days earlier, the pre-date Copernicus and NESRA used, rather than a clearer post-monsoon 2025 or April 2026 image: monsoon-to-monsoon means phenology cancels, and, decisively, it places the 8 July 2025 Rasuwagadhi GLOF damage in BOTH images so that prior event cancels rather than being mistaken for this one. A dry-season baseline would also invert the sign over farmland (NDVI lower in A than B) and under-detect. (d) maxCloud is 85 because the tile-wide cloud of the only post-event scene is 78.5%; that number is honest about the tile and misleading about the AOI, which is 92% clear — this AOI was chosen precisely because it is the clear hole in that scene. WHY BETRAWATI AND NOT THE HEADLINE SITES. The destruction reported at Rasuwagadhi, Timure and Syabrubesi is NOT usable on this pair: measured over their own bboxes, joint clear sky is 44.1% at Rasuwagadhi-Timure and 53.6% at Syabrubesi, and a full replay there returns 1000-2300 ha 'patches' that are compact cloud blobs, not scars — the event brief's own note that ~4.1 km of the assessed reach was cloud-obscured on 27 Aug is confirmed at pixel level and is worse than it sounds. Betrawati, ~40 km down the corridor by waypoint chain, is the one named impact site under clear sky on the only post-event pass. A September 2026 scene would allow an upper-gorge preset; none exists yet. WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW. 10 m NDVI sees stripped valley floor and nothing else: the 32-41 destroyed bridges, the ~40 km of swept Pasang Lhamu Highway, the Timure dry port, the damaged hydropower (901 MW affected), the buildings, and of course the ~788 dead and ~2,500 missing are all invisible here. Nor can imagery alone separate this surge from ordinary monsoon flooding on a river that is in flood every August — the magnitude (channel and bar area more than doubling in fifteen days) is the argument, not the detection itself. Caveats: the pipeline reads no SCL, so ~20% of the reported hectares is cloud/shadow; the largest patch is only 86% SCL-clear because 13% of it classifies as 'dark', which is what wet scoured sand in an incised channel looks like; and the AOI's southern edge sits ~500 m north of the limit of MGRS-45RUM's valid data, so enlarging it southward would introduce nodata.
